     - CMake
     - pFUnit
     - gfortran

# What is a unit test?

“If the parts don’t work by themselves, they probably won’t work well together”

(Thomas and Hunt, 2019,
[The pragmatic programmer](https://search.worldcat.org/search?q=bn:9780135957059),
Topic 51).

## Definition of a unit test

::: {.column-page}

::: {.column}

Unit tests are:

- Isolated
- Minimal
- Fast
- tests which verify the correctness of a single unit of code.

:::

::: {.column}

Benefits of unit tests:

- Confidence that your code does what you expect.
- Easier to make changes to you code.
- Catch bugs before they are introduced.

:::

:::

# Temperature conversions library

Throughout this workshop you will be writing tests for the
[temperature conversion library provided in the exercises](https://github.com/carpentries-incubator/fortran-unit-testing/tree/main/exercises/writing-your-first-unit-test/challenge).

# Our first unit test

## Testing the temperature {.smaller}

First, how can we test this library using standard Fortran?

::: {.fragment}

[solution/standard_fortran/test_temp_conversions.f90](https://github.com/carpentries-incubator/fortran-unit-testing/blob/main/exercises/writing-your-first-unit-test/solution/standard_fortran/test_temp_conversions.f90)

:::

::: {.fragment .column-page}

What makes this implementation good? What makes it bad?

::: {.column}

Good:

- The tests are partially parameterise
- Good failure logs

:::

::: {.column}

Bad:

- Unable to run a single test in isolation.
- Extra maintenance of test runner logic.
- Do not benefit from community development efforts

:::

:::

# Our first pFUnit test

## Why are we using pFUnit?

**Supports testing MPI parallelised code**, including parameterising tests by
number of MPI ranks.

::: {.fragment}

A few other reasons:

- The most feature rich framework.
- The most widely used framework.
- Being maintained.
- Dedicated CMake and Make integrations.

:::

## Standard Fortran to pFUnit

### [Live coding example](https://carpentries-incubator.github.io/fortran-unit-testing/instructor/pfunit-basics.html)

Starting with the standard Fortran test we saw earlier, follow along writing
tests for the temperature conversion library.

## Building with CMake

### [Live code example](https://carpentries-incubator.github.io/fortran-unit-testing/instructor/integrating-with-build-systems.html#integrating-pfunit-with-cmake)

along to build your newly written pFUnit test of the temperature conversion

# Parameterising with pFUnit

## Why bother parameterising?

- No repeated test logic.
- pFUnit handles reporting failed tests.
- Ensures the full test suite runs.
